# Overview

## Logline

A scale-house clerk in a Maine harbor town keeps the books on a trade she knows is
ending, while her brother cuts a full pond to prove it is not.

## Premise

Natural ice paid for the town for forty years. Electric refrigeration takes the
domestic trade first and the fish trade last, and the family that owns the pond
argues about the difference between a bad year and the last year.

## Themes

- What a ledger knows before anybody says it out loud.
- Risk taken on behalf of a memory.

## Tone

Dry, close, working. Weather is a condition, not a mood.

## Structure

Two acts, 1929 to 1942, chronological.
